class.name: JoinPayload
class.brief_description: What a player asks to join a session with.
class.description: A client fills one of these and hands it to [method NetwConnector.join], [method MultiplayerTree.host_player], or [method NetwConnector.join_or_host]. Where to connect is a [NetwConnectTarget] and is not part of this, so the same payload joins any target. It is a request rather than a fact. The server reads it from bytes the client wrote, overwrites [member peer_id] with the peer it actually assigned, and only then runs its join gate, which is what turns it into a [ResolvedJoin]. Nothing downstream of admission reads this. [codeblock] var payload := JoinPayload.new() payload.username = &"valeria" payload.arg_values = [best_lap] connector.join(target, payload) [/codeblock]

method.name: deserialize
method.description: Reads this payload from [param bytes], answering whether they spelled a request. [param bytes] come from a peer that has not been admitted yet, so this refuses rather than trusting: bytes that are not a record, a record missing [member username] or [member peer_id], and a [member peer_id] that is not a number all answer [code]false[/code]. A refused read writes nothing, so a payload that was reused is left exactly as it was rather than holding half of a rejected request.

method.name: resolve
method.description: Turns this request into the accepted join it describes, or [code]null[/code] when [member username] is empty. [member arg_values] is copied deeply, so the caller may keep mutating its own array without moving what was admitted.

method.name: serialize
method.description: Writes the request as the frame that travels to the server, carrying [member arg_bytes] rather than [member arg_values].

members.member: The wire form of [member arg_values], packed by the session against its resolved handler's schema. Empty when there is no join intent.

Typed join args the session's registered handler receives after the [ResolvedJoin], filled by the client from that handler's wire schema. This field itself never rides the wire: the session encodes it into [member arg_bytes] before the request travels.
Whether this connection was initiated with debug initialization data.
The peer this request belongs to. The server assigns it from the sender it actually received the frame from, so a client filling it in changes nothing.
Names the schema [member arg_bytes] was packed against, so a client and a server that disagree about the join handler's signature are rejected rather than misread.
The display name to spawn this player under. A request with none resolves to no join.
